newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo, SmithKline set record highs.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo, SmithKline set record highs.

text.p: Shares in Glaxo Wellcome Plc, SmithKline Beecham Plc and Zeneca Group Plc all leapt to to record highs on Tuesday as renewed investment demand caught the market short of stock, dealers and analysts said.

Spurred by gains in their ADRs in New York, Glaxo was up 53-1/2p at 12.65 stg by 1049 GMT in trade of just over four million shares, SmithKline climbed 57p to 10.99 stg in volume of 3.6 million and Zeneca was up 48-1/2p at 19.91-1/2 stg in thin trade of just over half a million shares.
"We have just seen loads and loads of buyers," said one market maker, "investors seem to love the sector, I think it is a bit of herd instinct."
Analysts said the drug sector could be in demand because of long-term positive factors, highlighted by recent hopes in the U.S. that inflation was unlikely to pick up anytime soon.

"In a low inflation environment, what you want to be invested in is a sector with solid top-line momentum, and you can't do better in that respect than the pharmaceuticals," said Peter Cartwright, analyst at Williams de Broe.
"And as the economy gets richer and older, you can't do better than the pharmaceuticals."

Cartwright also highlighted a report in Business Week magazine that death rates for AIDS patients were plummeting under the impact of combination drug therapies -- expanding the market for anti-AIDS drugs where Glaxo in particular is a leader.
Patients living longer create a potentially lucrative market for expensive AIDS therapies -- which Business Week said can cost as much as $15,000 a year per patient.

Other analysts said the UK drug sector was being re-rated to bring it in line with international peers, and that there was a growing enthusiasm among U.S. investors for European stocks amid nervousness over the ratings on some U.S. stocks.
BZW analyst Steve Plag said the drug sector was being re-rated worldwide.
"There has been a general realisation over the past 12 months that the industry has undergone a fundamental change in its technology base and a sea change in productivity," Plag said.
He said that with U.S. and UK economic growth also looking less certain, drug firms were benefitting from their defensive appeal.
Plag added that drug companies drew a comparison with the sector's rating in the mid-80's, when he said the drug majors traded at premiums of up to 70 percent to the rest of the market.
He said the UK's big three were currently at a premium of between 50 and 65 percent, "and that is not outlandish".

Market sources said analysts at NatWest were positive on growth prospects at SmithKline following a meeting with the company, but continued to rate the stock "hold" because of its high market valuation.

"NatWest is talking about 15 percent earnings growth and there are no U.S. patent expiries until after the year 2000," said one dealer. "Good earnings growth will sustain it into the next century." -- David Holmes and Jonathan Birt, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4367
